metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Photo rotation (r / Shift+R), non-persistent
tasks.description: Rotate the current photo 90 degrees clockwise (r) and counter-clockwise (Shift+R). Each altered photo's orientation is remembered in RAM only and discarded when the app closes.
tasks.details: DONE. Rotation quadrant lives on ViewTransform (pb-render::view) with cw/ccw stepping + UV remap + w/h swap for fit; unit-tested (4x cw = identity). Per-image overrides in an in-RAM HashMap<item, Rotation> (privacy task #2); identity drops the entry. r/Shift+R bound (Shift tracked via ModifiersChanged). Applied as a GPU transform on the quad - perf-neutral, no re-decode. NOTE: a golden-image rotation render test is deferred (geometry is unit-tested instead).
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the rotation state machine (cw wraps 0->1->2->3->0; ccw reverses). Extend pb-render fit tests for the w/h-swapped fit recompute. Property test: four cw rotations return to the original. Golden-image test: a rotated render matches its reference within tolerance.

tasks.title: Privacy: no persistent caches, no disk traces
tasks.description: Keep zero persistent caches and no on-disk metadata. Nothing about what was viewed survives the process; once cleared there is no trace of what you were looking at.
tasks.details: A cross-cutting design constraint, best baked in early rather than retrofitted. No thumbnail DB, no recent-files list, no config writes of viewed paths, no temp files of decoded pixels. Every cache - the compressed-byte LRU, the decoded ring, VRAM textures, rotation/zoom overrides (Tasks 1/3), and on-demand metadata reads (Task 5) - is RAM-backed and dropped on exit (Task 6). If on-disk scratch is ever required it must be opt-in and explicitly cleared. No logging of viewed paths to disk by default. This is partly principle (enforced in review) and partly verifiable (the no-trace test).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration 'no-trace' test: run a view session pointed at a sandbox and assert (via before/after filesystem diff) that no files are created or modified outside the binary's own directories. Static audit: no disk-write APIs on the view/cache hot paths; all caches are RAM-backed types. Document the guarantee in CLAUDE.md.

tasks.title: Zoom in/out (+ / -), including below fit
tasks.description: + and - zoom the current photo about its center. Zooming out can go smaller than the screen bounds (under-fit), not just larger.
tasks.details: DONE (zoom + pan). Zoom scalar (clamped 0.05x-32x) + pan offset on ViewTransform; perf-neutral GPU transforms, reset per photo. =/+ and numpad+ zoom in, -/numpad- out; HOLD-TO-ZOOM with a time-based exponential acceleration ramp (gentle start for fine tuning, faster the longer held) applied in about_to_wait. PAN added in the same change (owner request): arrow keys pan around the photo, same accel ramp, clamped to image bounds (max_pan in pb-render::view); arrows no longer advance (space=next, backspace=prev). Tier-2 re-decode when zoomed past native is deferred (GPU-scaled for now). Zoom-about-pan-focus (vs center) is a noted refinement.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure tests on zoom math: factor stepping, clamping at bounds, center-preserving transform. Property: N zoom_in steps then N zoom_out steps returns to baseline within epsilon. Golden-image tests at representative zoom levels (incl. under-fit).

tasks.title: Scaling modes: 0 original, 8 fit (default), 9 fill
tasks.description: Number keys choose the scaling mode: 0 = pixel-for-pixel original centered on screen, 8 = fit-to-screen (default, no crop), 9 = fill the screen (crop the overflowing edges).
tasks.details: DONE. The shared per-photo ViewTransform (pb-render::view) composes mode + rotation + zoom + pan and is unit-tested; the renderer draws from it (rotation/zoom/pan are perf-neutral GPU transforms). cover_rect/original_rect added next to fit_rect. Keys 0/8/9 bound to Original/Fit/Fill. DEVIATION from the original plan: mode is GLOBAL/sticky (set once, applies as you browse) rather than per-photo non-persistent - better UX for a flick-viewer. Fill & Original decode full-res (so Fill isn't upscale-blurry); the byte-budgeted ring bounds VRAM. A mode change bumps the geometry epoch and re-buffers neighbors.
tasks.testStrategy: Extend pb-render fit tests: cover() fully covers the screen and crops while preserving aspect; original() is exactly native size, centered (offsets may be negative). Property tests: Fill output covers the whole viewport; Fit output never exceeds it; Original equals native dimensions. Golden-image test per mode.

tasks.title: Metadata HUD panel (I, Shift+I, I-off)
tasks.description: I toggles a translucent dark-tinted panel on the screen edge showing date / mtime / dimensions / image format. Shift+I shows full EXIF for nerds. Pressing I again hides it.
tasks.details: Builds the reusable translucent HUD/overlay layer also used by the help card (Task 7). Render an alpha-blended dark panel anchored to a screen edge with text. Basic view: filename, file mtime, capture date (EXIF DateTimeOriginal), pixel dimensions, format. Full view (Shift+I): all EXIF tags, scrollable. Privacy (Task 2): read EXIF on demand from the in-RAM file bytes; never cache it to disk. Needs text rendering (a small glyph atlas / bitmap font). Three-state toggle: off -> basic -> (Shift+I) full -> off. Register actions info_toggle / info_full (Task 8).
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test EXIF extraction (basic field set + full tag map) against fixture images. Unit-test the toggle state machine (off/basic/full transitions). Golden-image test the panel layout + translucency. Privacy test: the metadata read writes nothing to disk.

tasks.title: Esc: immediate close, then clean teardown
tasks.description: Pressing Esc immediately closes the photo and the application, cleaning up after itself once it is no longer visible.
tasks.details: On Esc, hide/close the window FIRST for an instant perceived exit, then run teardown: drop the VRAM ring, the byte LRU, decoded buffers, rotation/zoom overrides, and any metadata - implementing the privacy guarantee (Task 2). No flush-to-disk on exit. Ordering matters: the visual close happens before the heavy frees so quitting always feels instant. Register action quit (Task 8).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration test: teardown frees/zeroes caches and the process exits 0, creating no files (shares the no-trace assertion with Task 2). Manual/perf check: the window is gone within ~1 frame of Esc.

tasks.title: Configurable keybindings (TOML)
tasks.description: Make keyboard shortcuts configurable via a TOML file, with sensible built-in defaults and a central action dispatch.
tasks.details: Define a central set of named actions: next, prev, random, rotate_cw, rotate_ccw, zoom_in, zoom_out, zoom_reset, mode_original, mode_fit, mode_fill, info_toggle, info_full, help_toggle, quit (extend as features land). Parse a TOML keybindings file into an action->keys map; embed defaults so it works with no file. TOML is chosen over YAML for simplicity and Rust ecosystem fit (serde + toml). Privacy (Task 2): config is read-only input - never write viewed state to it. Validate bindings (warn on unknown action or duplicate key). The keymap is the single source of truth that the help overlay (Task 7) reads. Decide config discovery (next to the binary, or an explicit --config path) with no implicit writes. All keyboard features (Tasks 1,3,4,5,6,7) register their actions here and become remappable once this lands.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test TOML parsing into the action map: valid config, invalid config (clear error), partial override merges over defaults. Property: defaults + empty config == defaults. Test conflict detection (duplicate key, unknown action). Round-trip the embedded default config.

tasks.title: Recursive directory mode (R)
tasks.description: R toggles recursive mode: the playlist spans the current directory plus every subfolder, ordered so a folder's own photos show first, then each subfolder in order, recursively - i.e. roughly full-path order.
tasks.details: When recursive mode is on, the scan walks the whole tree and rebuilds the playlist. ORDERING (confirm with owner): directory-grouped depth-first - within a directory its own images come first (natural/numeric sort so img2 < img10), then descend into each subdirectory in natural order, recursively. This differs subtly from a pure lexicographic full-path sort (where a file 'z.jpg' would sort after a subfolder 'a/'); the grouped traversal matches the owner's 'current dir's photos first, then each subfolder'. REBUILD: the app owns the ordered path list while pb-core Playlist holds count + index, so toggling re-scans, re-sorts, rebuilds Playlist (and its precomputed shuffle for the new length), and keeps the current photo by re-finding its new index. PRIVACY (Task 2): scanning reads directory entries only - no on-disk index is written. Use walkdir; skip unreadable dirs; guard against symlink loops. KEY CONFLICT: 'R' (Shift+R) was assigned to rotate-CCW in Task 1 - recommend recursive=R and moving rotate-CCW to another default (trivial via Task 8); confirm with owner.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the path-ordering function over a synthetic tree: a folder's files precede its subfolders' files, folders appear in natural order, natural (numeric) sort holds within a folder. Test toggle on/off keeps the current photo (index re-found). Edge cases: empty subdirs, non-image files filtered out, unreadable dirs skipped.

tasks.title: Transient command-feedback toast (white text, dark shadow)
tasks.description: When a command is invoked, briefly flash a translucent message on screen for feedback - white text with dark shadows/outline so it stays legible over any photo.
tasks.details: A transient 'toast' overlay that appears on command invocation and fades after a short timeout (~0.8-1.2s). Reuses the HUD/text-rendering layer from Task 5. White text with a dark drop-shadow or outline for legibility over light AND dark images. Each action emits a short message - e.g. 'Rotate CW', 'Fill', 'Recursive: on', 'Zoom 150%', 'Random'. Sourced from the central action dispatch (Task 8) so any action can register a feedback string. Perf-neutral: a small text quad drawn for a few frames, fading via alpha; a new command replaces the current toast. PRIVACY (Task 2): messages are transient and never logged to disk. Pick a default anchor (e.g. bottom-center).
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test the toast state/timer logic: show, time-based alpha decay, replace-on-new-command, expire. Golden-image test the rendered toast (white text + dark shadow) on both light and dark backgrounds for legibility. Test that representative actions emit the expected message strings.
